portrait-of-inaida-gippius

A young woman with a serious look is shown in the rich, graceful style of Léon Bakst, a Jewish Russian artist. Zinaida Gippius was a famous Russian poet and writer in Saint Petersburg, and Bakst painted her as part of the lively circle of artists he belonged to. The portrait shows his skill with line and color. It's a picture of a creative friendship.
merry-go-round

People whirl on a fairground carousel in a blaze of bold, swirling color, painted as if everything is spinning at once. Mark Gertler, a British painter whose Jewish parents came from Poland, made this during World War I, as a bitter picture of people being swept around by forces they can't stop. The harsh colors and rounded shapes make it unforgettable. It's regarded as his masterpiece.
recha-welcoming-her-father-detail

A woman greets her father at the door in a warm, joyful family scene. Maurycy Gottlieb, a Jewish painter from Galicia, studied under the great Polish painter Jan Matejko. He painted this when he was only in his early twenties; he died at 22, but left behind a few remarkable paintings.
self-portrait-in-polish-nobleman-s-dress

Gottlieb, a young Jewish painter, dresses himself as a Polish nobleman, wearing a fur-trimmed coat and a fur hat. He painted this when he was about 20 as a way of saying that Jews were also a part of Polish culture. The proud pose and rich costume are meant to be a statement. It's one of the best-known self-portraits in Polish-Jewish art.
ahasuerus

A tall, weary traveler walks through a dark landscape, in a picture of the legendary Wandering Jew, a man condemned to roam forever. Maurycy Gottlieb painted Ahasuerus as a lonely, noble figure. He gave a sad folk legend a feeling of dignity. It shows how Jewish artists reworked old stories.
jews-praying-in-the-synagogue-on-yom-kippur

Worshippers stand and pray in a crowded synagogue on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the Jewish year. Maurycy Gottlieb painted this near the end of his short life and included himself in the picture as one of the men standing among them. Each face is different and carefully painted. It's the most famous painting of Jewish prayer and a treasure in the Tel Aviv Museum of Art.
christ-preaching-at-capernaum

Jesus speaks to a crowd in Capernaum, with Jewish listeners gathered around him. Maurycy Gottlieb, a Jewish painter, imagined Jesus as a Jewish teacher in a Jewish town. He painted it in the last year of his life. It shows how a Jewish artist could look at a Gospel story as part of his own culture.
women-plucking-geese

Women in a simple farmhouse sit together plucking geese, with the feathers floating in the sunlight. Max Liebermann, a Jewish painter from Berlin, was just starting out when he painted this large picture of ordinary labor. Some critics were shocked by the plain subject. It launched his career as a painter of working people.
the-twelve-year-old-jesus-in-the-temple

A boy Jesus speaks with scholars in a temple, with a look of calm. Max Liebermann painted Jesus as a Jewish boy among Jewish teachers, which was shocking to some people in 1879 who wanted him portrayed in a more traditional way. The painting caused a big controversy in Germany. It shows how Liebermann challenged expectations from the start.
free-period-in-the-amsterdam-orphanage

Girls in black and white dresses and caps rest and chat in the sunny courtyard of an orphanage in Amsterdam. Max Liebermann painted this when visiting the Netherlands, where he admired the work of Dutch masters. The play of light and shade through the trees is lovely. It's one of his best-known early works.
cobbler-s-shop

A cobbler sits and works at his bench in a small shop, surrounded by shoes and tools. Max Liebermann was fascinated by workers and their daily tasks. The warm, gloomy light and the careful composition show his respect for the craft. It's a quiet picture of a simple trade.
the-bleaching-ground

Women spread linen to bleach in the sunshine across a meadow in the Netherlands. Max Liebermann loved the quiet beauty of country work, which he studied during long stays in Holland. The wide landscape and bright light are very peaceful. It's a classic of German-Dutch realism.
munich-beer-garden

Families sit at tables under chestnut trees in a Bavarian beer garden, with sunlight shimmering through the leaves. Max Liebermann painted this in Munich and later became the leading German Impressionist. He liked to paint people enjoying leisure. It's a cheerful scene of German life.
amsterdamer-waisenmadchen-im-garten

Orphan girls sit and walk together in a leafy garden, in the dappled sunshine. This is another version of the orphanage garden theme Max Liebermann loved. He painted it again and again in different lights. It shows his love for the way the light moves through leaves.
the-garden-of-the-amsterdam-orphanage

Girls in simple uniforms rest and walk in the shade of old trees, with spots of sunlight on the ground. Max Liebermann painted the orphanage garden many times, and each version is a study of light and shade. His loose brushwork is typical of his later Impressionist period. It's a peaceful, lovely scene.
portrait-of-the-painter-lovis-corinth

A sturdy man with a stern, serious look sits at his easel, painted in strong dark strokes. Lovis Corinth was a fellow German artist and Liebermann's colleague, though they often disagreed. Liebermann, a leader of the Berlin Secession, painted many portraits of colleagues. It's a fair look at a great painter.
der-hamburgische-professorenkonvent

A group of professors in black robes sit around a table, discussing business, in a group portrait. Max Liebermann was asked to paint the University of Hamburg's professors, and he gave each one a lively, individual look. It shows his gift for capturing character. It's a notable German group portrait.
villa-in-hilversum

A garden with a country house shines in the sun with bright colors, with leafy trees and flowers. Max Liebermann painted the gardens he visited in the Netherlands, which he loved for the brilliance of the light. The picture is bright and happy. It's a good example of his late Impressionist style.
the-terrace-at-the-hotel-louis-c-jacob-in-nienstedten-o

Guests relax at tables on a shady terrace overlooking the Elbe River, with the sun speckling through trees. Max Liebermann painted this scene in the hotel that is still there in Hamburg today. The light and the leisurely mood are lovely. It's a gem of German Impressionism.
moses-with-the-tablets-of-the-law

Moses holds the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments, with a calm and strong face. Moritz Daniel Oppenheim, often called the first Jewish painter of modern Germany, painted this early in his career. It was a way of showing Jewish heritage with pride in a time when Jews had few rights. It's an important early work by a pioneer.
marriage-portrait-of-charlotte-de-rothschild

A young bride in a rich wedding gown is shown in a loving portrait. Moritz Daniel Oppenheim was a favorite painter of the Rothschild family, the famous Jewish banking family. He painted it with great care for rich fabrics and jewelry. It's a window into the elegant world of 19th-century Jewish high society.
lavater-and-lessing-visit-moses-mendelssohn

A group of men gather in a study for a friendly but serious debate, with the Jewish philosopher Moses Mendelssohn at the center. Oppenheim painted a famous meeting between Mendelssohn and two Christian thinkers, a story about respect and tolerance. It was an important message for German Jews in the 1800s. It's a famous image in Jewish history.
sabbath-rest

A Jewish family rests on the Sabbath in a warm home, with candles and a quiet mood. Moritz Daniel Oppenheim became famous for a series of paintings showing traditional Jewish family life. Many of his pictures were turned into prints and hung in homes across Europe. It's a loving look at a day of rest.
the-wandering-jew

A weary figure walks across a landscape strewn with the bones of others, past burning cities and fleeing people. Samuel Hirszenberg, a Jewish painter from Łódź in Poland, painted this huge picture as a sad vision of the history of persecution. It's a dramatic and sorrowful image. It hangs in the Israel Museum.
exile

A crowd of weary people trudge in a long line across a snowy plain, carrying children and belongings. Samuel Hirszenberg painted the suffering of Jewish families forced from their homes, based on the real events of his time. It's a powerful picture of a hard chapter of history. It reminds us of the resilience of people.
an-early-reading-of-shakespeare

A group of people gather around a young Shakespeare as he reads aloud a play. Solomon Hart was an English painter and the first Jewish member of the Royal Academy. He painted scenes from history and literature in great detail. It's a warm tribute to the power of storytelling.
milton-visiting-galileo-when-a-prisoner-of-the-inquisit

The English poet John Milton visits the aging Italian astronomer Galileo, who is held under house arrest by the Inquisition. Solomon Hart, the first Jewish member of the Royal Academy, painted this scene of two great minds meeting. It celebrates the courage of thinking freely. It's a moving image.
binding-of-isaac

The Bible story in which Abraham is told to offer up his son Isaac, but an angel stops him at the last moment. Yosef Zvi Geiger was an artist born in Jerusalem during the Ottoman era. He painted it in a straightforward, heartfelt way. It's a rare early painting by an artist born in the Holy Land.
deep-in-the-woods

A shady forest path in dim light, painted with tall trees and soft moss. Aaron Allan Edson was a Canadian landscape painter from Quebec who loved the woods and mountains. His paintings celebrate the wilderness of eastern Canada and New England. It's a calm view of the forest.
a-scene-in-the-white-mountains

Mountains rise above a quiet valley, with the soft light of dawn or dusk. Aaron Allan Edson painted landscapes in Quebec and the White Mountains of New Hampshire. He was part of a generation of Canadian painters who showed the beauty of the land. It's a peaceful wilderness view.
julie-papineau-nee-bruneau-and-her-daughter-ezilda

A mother and her young daughter pose in their best clothes. Antoine Plamondon was one of Quebec's most important early portrait painters, and he painted leaders and their families. Julie Papineau was the wife of a famous political leader, Louis-Joseph Papineau. It's an elegant picture of a family from French Canada.
abigail-towne

A girl in a ruffled dress and cap sits calmly for her portrait. Antoine Plamondon, an early Canadian painter from Quebec, trained in Paris and returned to paint portraits of the middle class and religious figures. His faces are simple and honest. It's a portrait from early Canadian art.
les-petits-jardiniers

Two small children dig and plant in a garden, with their gardening tools. Antoine Plamondon, a Quebec painter, made this charming scene of childhood. It's one of his less formal pictures. It shows how Canadian painters also painted scenes of everyday life.
l-assemblee-des-six-comtes

A large crowd gathers in a field in Quebec in 1837 for a famous political meeting. It was an important event in the Rebellion of 1837 in Lower Canada. Charles Alexander Smith painted it decades later to remember the struggle. It's a snapshot of Canadian history.
monseigneur-antoine-adolphe-gauvreau

A church leader in rich robes sits in a dignified pose. Charles Huot was a well-known Quebec painter who made historical paintings and large decorations for the Quebec legislature. This portrait shows his skill with serious, formal subjects. It's an example of French-Canadian portraiture.
le-conseil-souverain

Officials in wigs and robes gather around a big table in the early government of New France. Charles Huot painted this huge scene of Canadian history, which hangs in the Quebec legislature. It shows how the French colony of Canada was governed in the 1600s. It's a grand history painting.
ole

A crowd cheers at a bullfight in Spain, with bright colors and festive costumes. Clarence Gagnon, a Quebec painter, traveled widely in Europe and painted scenes of Spain. The title is the Spanish shout of praise. It shows that Canadian artists also painted the world.
brise-d-ete-a-dinard

A summer breeze fills the sails of boats and the clothes of walkers on the seaside at Dinard in France, in bright sunlight. Clarence Gagnon painted this in his early career in France. The quick brushwork is lively. It's a happy seaside picture.
le-pont-de-glace-a-quebec

People cross the frozen St. Lawrence River at Quebec on an ice bridge in winter. Clarence Gagnon loved to paint Quebec's snow, villages and winter life. In cold winters the river froze solid, and people could walk across. It's a cheerful picture of Canadian winter.
a-north-american-indian-woman

A portrait of an Indigenous woman in traditional dress. Cornelius Krieghoff, a Dutch-born painter who lived in Quebec, painted many scenes of First Nations people. His pictures are an important record of life in the 1800s, though they show how a settler artist saw Indigenous people. It's a picture to study with care.
an-officer-s-room-in-montreal

A cozy room with an officer's belongings, bed and gear, in the glow of lamplight. Cornelius Krieghoff painted this in his early years in Montreal, when many British officers lived there. It gives a close look at daily life in Canada in the 1840s. It's a charming interior.
a-north-american-indian-hunter

An Indigenous hunter stands in a forest with his rifle, in a quiet pose. Cornelius Krieghoff painted First Nations people he met near Montreal and Quebec. The scene shows him in the setting of his daily life. It's part of a body of work that is important for Canadian history.
autumn-landscape

A forest is ablaze with red, orange and gold leaves beside a calm stream. Cornelius Krieghoff painted the glorious color of Canadian autumn, which became a favorite subject. The warm colors make the picture glow. It's a good example of his love of the Canadian landscape.
bilking-the-toll

A sleigh speeds away from a tollgate as the toll keeper shouts after it, in a snowy scene full of fun. Cornelius Krieghoff's lively scenes of French-Canadian country life made him one of Canada's most popular painters. It's a funny story told in a picture. It shows his eye for humor.
chippewas-hunting-caribou

Anishinaabe (Chippewa) hunters track caribou across a snowy landscape. Cornelius Krieghoff painted this to show the life he'd seen in the northern wilderness. The sweeping view and tiny figures show how large the land was. It's an important image of Indigenous hunting.
canoe-on-the-river

A birchbark canoe glides along a calm river between wooded banks. Krieghoff painted this scene of paddlers on a Canadian river, a very Canadian image. The calm water reflects the colorful trees. It's a peaceful scene of travel.
coastal-landscape-at-moonlight

A bright moon shines over a rocky coast and calm sea, painting a silver path on the water. Cornelius Krieghoff painted many moonlit scenes that were popular with buyers. The mood is dreamy. It's a quiet night view.
camp-scene-at-night

People gather around a campfire in the woods at night, with the flames lighting the trees. Cornelius Krieghoff painted the glow of firelight with great skill. The picture feels warm and cozy against the dark forest. It's a favorite style of his.
billboards

A city street scene of tall buildings and giant signs, in a bold, simple style. David Milne was a Canadian painter who lived in New York and later in Ontario. He made pictures of cities, signs, and nature with clean shapes and a light touch. It's an early work from his time in New York.
black

A quiet, simple painting in dark tones, with bold shapes. David Milne painted both in New York and in the Canadian woods, always using a thin, delicate touch. He is now considered one of Canada's most important modern painters. It's an early example of his inventive style.
dark-pool-ti-magami

A still, dark pool in the forest of Temagami in northern Ontario, with trees and rocks. David Milne painted the Canadian wilderness in thin, delicate watercolors. The mirror-like pool is quiet and mysterious. It's a peaceful picture of northern Ontario.
breton-church

A stone church stands in a village in Brittany, France, painted in warm, soft colors. Emily Carr, a Canadian painter from British Columbia, studied in France in the early 1900s. She was inspired by the strong colors and shapes of French painting. It's from the years before she became known for her Pacific Coast paintings.
breton-farm-yard

A farmyard in Brittany, with old buildings and the glow of sunlight. Emily Carr painted this during her time in France. The bright colors show she was learning from the modern painters there. She would later bring these lessons home to Canada.
autumn-in-france

Trees in fall colors line a country lane in France. Emily Carr studied in Paris and Brittany, and learned about the bright colors of Post-Impressionism. She painted this with a bold, free brush. It shows her artistic growth before returning to Canada.
first-nations-war-canoes-in-alert-bay

Large carved canoes sit on the beach of Alert Bay, a First Nations village on the coast of British Columbia. Emily Carr traveled to Indigenous villages along the Pacific Coast to paint and to record carvings and village life. She wanted to preserve what she saw. It's an important record of the West Coast in the early 1900s.
